abstract: The pangenome paradigm enables a more comprehensive capture of structural variants than traditional linear-reference-based approaches. Recent advances in graph-based pangenome construction and increasing availability of high-quality telomere-to-telomere assemblies now make it possible to represent genomic diversity more effectively, including structural rearrangements and intergenic regions that were previously underexplored. However, few tools allow researchers to interactively explore the complex landscape of a pangenome, particularly for large variation graphs. Here, we present PanAbyss, an application built around a novel data model that enables both the visualization of annotated graph segments and the identification and characterization of regions of interest. This approach allows PanAbyss to offer unique functionalities, including the ability to query a region by annotation, to search for regions shared among specific individuals in the graph, compute proximity trees between individuals, and retrieve sequences associated with targeted regions. PanAbyss thus provides a versatile and user-friendly platform for in-depth pangenome exploration. To illustrate its utility, we present a use case focusing on the identification of structural variants associated with the white head phenotype in cattle, and compare our findings to previously reported results.
